subsystems.name: Post-quantum signature scheme
subsystems.role: authenticates transactions so they cannot be forged by a quantum computer.
parts: key generation, signing and verification routines

subsystems.name: Ledger protocol
subsystems.role: defines how transactions and blocks are structured and validated.

subsystems.name: Key management
subsystems.role: generates, stores and uses the much larger private keys safely.

subsystems.name: Network layer
subsystems.role: propagates transactions and blocks between nodes.

subsystems.name: Migration and interoperability
subsystems.role: lets a ledger move from classical to post-quantum cryptography without splitting the network.

subsystems.name: Cryptographic agility
subsystems.role: allows algorithms to be swapped if weaknesses are later found.

buildSteps.title: Select algorithms
buildSteps.detail: Choose standardised post-quantum signature schemes (for example ML-DSA or SLH-DSA) based on security level, key and signature size, and verification speed.

buildSteps.title: Design the transaction format
buildSteps.detail: Extend the transaction structure to carry public keys and signatures that are kilobytes in size, versus tens of bytes for elliptic-curve signatures.

buildSteps.title: Implement verification
buildSteps.detail: Rewrite node software to verify the new signatures, optimising code so validation does not slow block processing too much.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with consensus
buildSteps.detail: Modify block validation rules to accept the new signature types, while keeping the chain consistent for nodes that have not yet upgraded.

buildSteps.title: Rework addresses
buildSteps.detail: Derive addresses from the new public keys, typically by hashing, so users keep short, collision-resistant identifiers.

buildSteps.title: Update wallets
buildSteps.detail: Add key generation, secure storage and signing for the larger keys into desktop, mobile and hardware wallets.

buildSteps.title: Plan the migration
buildSteps.detail: Run a hybrid mode where transactions must carry both a classical and a post-quantum signature, then schedule a cut-over height.

buildSteps.title: Test and audit
buildSteps.detail: Operate testnets, commission independent security audits, and benchmark throughput under realistic load.

buildSteps.title: Activate on the network
buildSteps.detail: Coordinate a software upgrade across miners, validators, exchanges and node operators, then monitor for forks or failures.

prerequisites.why: NIST finalised its first post-quantum standards in 2024, giving ledgers proven algorithms to build on.
post-quantum operations are slower and produce larger data, so hardware acceleration and bigger blocks may be needed.
hardware wallets and secure enclaves have limited space and must be updated to hold multi-kilobyte keys.
most ledgers hard-code their signature scheme, so adding a new one requires a carefully managed protocol change.
bigger signatures reduce the number of transactions per block, which may require layer-2 solutions or parameter changes.

pathway.milestone: NIST post-quantum standards published; niche ledgers such as the Quantum Resistant Ledger already use hash-based signatures like XMSS
pathway.unlocks: real, audited building blocks for quantum-resistant systems.

pathway.milestone: major ledgers deploy hybrid classical-plus-post-quantum signatures on testnets and then mainnet
pathway.unlocks: protection against quantum attack without forcing every user to switch at once.

pathway.milestone: full post-quantum migration for wallets, exchanges and smart contracts
pathway.unlocks: a ledger where no part of the transaction flow relies on breakable cryptography.

pathway.milestone: quantum-resistant consensus and cross-chain communication, possibly with quantum key distribution for high-value links
pathway.unlocks: end-to-end security even if large-scale quantum computers arrive.
